scenes.tts: How does a growing branch know which thin layer to stop in?
scenes.visual: Title card: Same Means Stick. A cross-section of retina; processes descend toward a stack of thin coloured bands.
scenes.narration: How does a growing branch know which thin layer to stop in?

scenes.tts: A gradient can bring an axon near its target. But a thin layer is either the right one or not.
scenes.visual: A smooth colour gradient brings axons to roughly the right region; zoom into a stack of thin bands, one lit as correct.
scenes.narration: A gradient can bring an axon near its target. But a thin layer is either the right one or not.

scenes.tts: Choices like that often call for discrete labels.
scenes.visual: Card: discrete choices, discrete labels.
scenes.narration: Choices like that often call for discrete labels.

scenes.tts: In the retina, the inner plexiform layer is a thin band where three kinds of cell make synapses.
scenes.visual: Retina cross-section. Label: inner plexiform layer. Bipolar, amacrine and retinal ganglion cells labelled; their processes meet in the band.
scenes.narration: In the retina, the inner plexiform layer is a thin band where three kinds of cell make synapses.

scenes.tts: It is divided into thinner sublaminae. Each cell type sends its processes into one or a few.
scenes.visual: The band splits into thin coloured sublaminae. Each cell type's processes end in one or two of them. A process ending in the wrong band meets the wrong partners; a red mark. Schematic.
scenes.narration: It is divided into thinner sublaminae. Each cell type sends its processes into one or a few.

scenes.tts: In chick retina, two related proteins are Sidekick one and Sidekick two.
scenes.caption: In chick retina, two related proteins are Sidekick-1 and Sidekick-2.
scenes.visual: Two cell groups light up in two colours, labelled Sidekick-1 and Sidekick-2. Chick retina.
scenes.narration: In chick retina, two related proteins are Sidekick-1 and Sidekick-2.

scenes.tts: Largely separate groups of neurons make them. Each group's processes end in different sublaminae.
scenes.visual: Processes of the Sidekick-1 group end in one band, the Sidekick-2 group in another.
scenes.narration: Largely separate groups of neurons make them. Each group's processes end in different sublaminae.

scenes.tts: Each protein binds its own kind, which is called homophilic binding.
scenes.visual: Close-up: two membranes zip together where identical proteins meet. Label: homophilic binding.
scenes.narration: Each protein binds its own kind, which is called homophilic binding.

scenes.tts: Sidekick one sticks to Sidekick one.
scenes.caption: Sidekick-1 sticks to Sidekick-1.
scenes.visual: Two Sidekick-1 processes adhere; a Sidekick-2 process beside them does not.
scenes.narration: Sidekick-1 sticks to Sidekick-1.

scenes.tts: Does the label only mark the band, or help choose it?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: marks the band, or helps choose it?
scenes.narration: Does the label only mark the band, or help choose it?

scenes.tts: Predict. Make neurons produce a Sidekick they normally lack. Where should their processes end?
scenes.visual: On screen: Predict. A cell with no Sidekick is given Sidekick-1. Where does its arbor go?
scenes.narration: Predict. Make neurons produce a Sidekick they normally lack. Where should their processes end?

scenes.tts: Their processes shifted toward the sublamina where that Sidekick was already concentrated.
scenes.visual: The arbor drifts into the Sidekick-1 band. Label: misexpression. Credit: Yamagata, Weiner and Sanes, 2002.
scenes.narration: Their processes shifted toward the sublamina where that Sidekick was already concentrated.

scenes.tts: Adding the label shifted the arbor.
scenes.visual: Caption card: add the label, and the arbor shifts.
scenes.narration: Adding the label shifted the arbor.

scenes.tts: Later, Yamagata and Sanes added Dee-scam and Dee-scam L, making four labels.
scenes.caption: Later, Yamagata and Sanes added Dscam and DscamL, making four labels.
scenes.visual: Four proteins, four colours: Sidekick-1, Sidekick-2, Dscam, DscamL, each with its own group of cells and bands. Credit: 2008.
scenes.narration: Later, Yamagata and Sanes added Dscam and DscamL, making four labels.

scenes.tts: These molecules bias a choice. They are one part of how layers form.
scenes.visual: Caution card: a bias, not an address book.
scenes.narration: These molecules bias a choice. They are one part of how layers form.

scenes.tts: In mouse retina, cells lacking Dee-scam or Dee-scam-like one still reach the right sublaminae.
scenes.caption: In mouse retina, cells lacking DSCAM or DSCAML1 still reach the right sublaminae.
scenes.visual: Mouse retina panel: knockout cells' processes still end in the correct bands.
scenes.narration: In mouse retina, cells lacking DSCAM or DSCAML1 still reach the right sublaminae.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry through this lesson. A match between identical proteins says only, we are the same.
scenes.visual: Card line 1: a match says, we are the same.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry through this lesson. A match between identical proteins says only, we are the same.

scenes.tts: The cell decides what same means.
scenes.visual: Card line 2: the cell decides what same means.
scenes.narration: The cell decides what same means.

scenes.tts: When a group of cells shares a sticky label, their processes are drawn together.
scenes.visual: Card line 3: shared label plus stick draws like processes together, toward matching sublaminae.
scenes.narration: When a group of cells shares a sticky label, their processes are drawn together.

scenes.tts: Here, same means stick.
scenes.visual: The word stick is circled; beside it a faded word: retreat.
scenes.narration: Here, same means stick.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: in chick retina, shared sticky labels help like processes settle in matching sublaminae, alongside other cues.
scenes.visual: Closing card: shared sticky labels help like processes settle in matching sublaminae, alongside other cues.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: in chick retina, shared sticky labels help like processes settle in matching sublaminae, alongside other cues.
